label: copy-phase input b (previous output was b), from the 3rd output on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is the letter b (i.e. the model just output b) and the step is recall_idx >= 2. Essentially all activation (100% of mass) is on in_tok == b; no activation in the original phase or on the delimiter, and none on any other input token. At recall_idx 1 (b fed back right after the first copied token) it is nearly silent (rate 0.001 vs ~0.03 later). The output token, prev tokens, first token and repeat counts barely modulate the rate. About 11% of predicted b-input copy steps stay inactive with no obvious pattern in the misses; the few missed activations are weak ones where the sequence starts with b and b is fed back at recall_idx 1. Strongest examples have b fed back late in long sequences, often with a second b following, but I did not systematically check magnitude scaling.

issues: The core label and predicate hold up. I reproduced the reported test scores exactly: P 0.887, R 0.990, F1 0.936, mass recall 0.997. On dev, all activation is in the copy phase (none in the original phase or on the delimiter), and in_tok == b carries 66564 of 66565 active steps (the one exception is g).

The explanation says the false positives 'show no clear pattern'. That is false. Precision of the predicate falls systematically on the last copy step of short sequences: L=3 with to_go=0 is 0.33, L=4 with to_go=0 is 0.66, L=5 with to_go=0 is 0.75. For L>=6 it is about 0.91-0.94 at every to_go. L=3 overall is 0.33 and L=4 overall is 0.78. Precision also climbs with recall_idx and with absolute t: L=9 at recall_idx 2 is 0.83, against about 0.94-0.97 later. So the feature is weaker early and at the end of short sequences, rather than being cleanly on for every b input at recall_idx >= 2.

Excluding those cells does not improve F1. Excluding (to_go==0)&(L<=5) gives test F1 0.918, and excluding (to_go==0)&(L<=4) gives 0.930, both below 0.936. The effect is graded, so the original predicate is still the best simple boolean one. The defect is in the explanation, not the predicate.

The recall_idx 1 rates are quoted on mismatched bases. 0.001 at recall_idx 1 and 'about 0.03 at later steps' are rates over all input tokens. Conditioned on b being the input, the firing rate is about 0.05 at recall_idx 1 (L=9: 0.055, L=6: 0.047) against about 0.89 at recall_idx >= 2. The qualitative claim ('almost silent' at recall_idx 1) is right, but the numbers don't compare like with like.

Other claims check out. Out_tok, prev_tok, prev2_tok, first_tok and repeat counts barely matter (in_count>=2 gives precision 0.85 against 0.89 for in_count==1). The missed activations are weak and hold 0.3% of the mass. In the examples, most misses are b fed back at recall_idx 1 in sequences starting with b. One exception is a b fed back at recall_idx 1 in 'b j b 2 2 1 y i'.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input b (model just output b), from recall_idx 2 on; weaker and less reliable on the final step of short sequences (L<=5) and at early copy positions
